Good morning dispatchers,
Thanks for a steady run; the ramp coordinator noted a detail about kennel doors

I want us to keep that note front and center. When a kennel door feels even slightly off, we slow the handoff and check the latch, the seal, and the fit before the pet moves again. That is not fussing, that is care. Our travelers count on us to treat every crate like it carries somebody's family member, because it does.

For the next stretch, please keep the handoff notes crisp and push any concern upstream right away. If a passenger sounds uneasy, give them a calm answer, then loop in the supervisor without delay. If the pet is Poppy or any other traveler with special handling, make sure the booking record, the kennel tag, and the pickup plan all say the same thing. When a lane is crowded, we still choose safety over speed, and we do it without making the customer feel brushed aside. <<FACT F117>> Keep documenting the details clearly so we can protect the traveler and support the claim path if the situation calls for it.

Also, if a missed connection starts to build pressure at the counter, stay steady and keep the passenger updated while we sort the next move. <<FACT F110>> The best service here is simple: listen well, act fast, and leave no gap between what we promise and what the pet actually receives. If Ben Schneider or Caleb Silva comes through on a tight transfer, let the team know early so we can keep the animal calm and the route clean. That is how the Companion Animal Travel Desk earns trust day after day.
